tools.name: drain_node
tools.description: Cordons a node so nothing new is scheduled on it, then evicts the pods running there. Optionally leaves DaemonSet pods in place.

params.name: node_name
params.description: Name of the node to drain

params.name: grace_period_seconds
params.description: Grace period given to each evicted pod

tools.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from agents import function_tool
from kubernetes import client, config

config.load_kube_config()
_core = client.CoreV1Api()


@dataclass
class DrainResult:
    node: str
    cordoned: bool
    evicted: list = field(default_factory=list)
    skipped: list = field(default_factory=list)
    failed: list = field(default_factory=list)


@function_tool
def drain_node(node_name: str, skip_daemonsets: bool = True, grace_period_seconds: int = 30) -> DrainResult:
    result = DrainResult(node=node_name, cordoned=False)
    _core.patch_node(node_name, {"spec": {"unschedulable": True}})
    result.cordoned = True

    pods = _core.list_pod_for_all_namespaces(field_selector=f"spec.nodeName={node_name}")
    for pod in pods.items:
        name = f"{pod.metadata.namespace}/{pod.metadata.name}"
        owners = pod.metadata.owner_references or []
        if skip_daemonsets and any(o.kind == "DaemonSet" for o in owners):
            result.skipped.append(name)
            continue
        body = client.V1Eviction(
            metadata=client.V1ObjectMeta(name=pod.metadata.name, namespace=pod.metadata.namespace),
            delete_options=client.V1DeleteOptions(grace_period_seconds=grace_period_seconds),
        )
        try:
            _core.create_namespaced_pod_eviction(pod.metadata.name, pod.metadata.namespace, body)
            result.evicted.append(name)
        except client.ApiException as exc:
            result.failed.append(f"{name}: {exc.reason}")
    return result

tools.name: buy_node_reserved_capacity

tools.name: grant_namespace_role
tools.description: Binds a user, group, or service account to a ClusterRole within a single namespace by running kubectl create rolebinding. This gives the subject that role's permissions in the namespace.

params.name: namespace
params.description: Namespace in which to grant access

params.name: role
params.description: ClusterRole to bind: view, edit, or admin

params.name: subject_kind
params.description: Kind of subject: User, Group, or ServiceAccount

params.name: subject_name
params.description: Name of the user, group, or service account

params.name: sa_namespace
params.description: Namespace of the service account, required when the subject is a ServiceAccount
